drafts.title: For 11 years the highest IPL total was 263. Since 2024, teams have passed it eight times.
drafts.caption:
For 11 years the highest IPL total was 263. Since 2024, teams have passed it eight times.

Most people put that down to the Impact Player rule, so we compared the IPL with leagues that don't have it.

In 2022, IPL top orders scored about as fast as the top orders in the Blast, PSL, CPL and T20 internationals. In 2026 they scored 167 runs per 100 balls. Those four: 147.

Teams still use about eight batters an innings, only a fraction more than before, and batters 8 to 11 account for about a seventh of the extra runs. Our read: the extra batting mostly sits unused, but knowing it's there, everyone swings harder, the top three most of all.

Numbers from Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, men's T20, 2019 to 2026. Top order means batters 1 to 3; the T20 internationals are games between full members.

Keep the rule or scrap it?

#IPL #ImpactPlayer #CricketStats #FineMargins
drafts.x: The IPL's highest total stood at 263 for 11 years. Teams have passed it eight times since 2024. Against leagues without the Impact Player rule, the biggest gap is the top three: a strike rate of 167 in 2026, against 147 elsewhere. Teams still use about eight batters an innings.
drafts.note: Squads not checked yet (no squads.json from the handover).
drafts.script:
For eleven years, the highest total in IPL history was two sixty-three.
Since twenty twenty-four, teams have gone past it eight times.
A normal first innings used to be about one sixty. This year, two hundred.
Everyone blames the Impact Player rule. So we checked the leagues without it.
In twenty twenty-two, IPL top orders scored as fast as the rest. Then, a year into the rule, they took off.
Now they score about twenty runs more per hundred balls.
And the extra batting? Teams barely touch it. They use about eight batters an innings, a fraction more than before.
So the extra runs mostly aren't coming from the extra batter. Everyone swings harder knowing he's there, the top three most of all.

drafts.title: Is the most expensive buy at an IPL auction worth the money?
drafts.caption:
Is the most expensive buy at an IPL auction worth the money?

We took the three biggest buys at every IPL auction since 2018. 26 of them played, and 8 beat an average player: 31%. Of all the other players teams bought, nearly four in ten did.

Rishabh Pant went for ₹27 crore in 2025 and scored 269 runs. A year earlier, Shashank Singh cost ₹20 lakh and scored 354.

"Beat an average player" means wins added in the Fine Margins model, IPL auctions 2018 to 2026.

What's the worst big buy you remember?

drafts.title: India won the ODI series in New Zealand 3-1. New Zealand scored 285 more runs.
drafts.caption:
India won the ODI series in New Zealand 3-1. New Zealand scored 285 more runs.

India's first two wins were rain-shortened chases settled by DLS, and the Hamilton game was washed out without a ball bowled. Two games went the full distance. New Zealand won the first by 244 runs, and India won the last by 22 at Bay Oval on 15 November after being bowled out for 209.

Since 2002, two ODI series winners have been outscored by more: England against India in 2011 (by 335 runs) and South Africa in England in 2025 (by 331).

It is New Zealand's first home ODI series defeat since India won 4-1 there in 2019.

Did 3-1 flatter India?

items.title: POV: auction day
items.text:
POV: IPL auction day.
You've got twenty-seven crore and the biggest paddle.
Your analyst waves a spreadsheet.
You wave back.
Sold! Confetti! The room goes wild.
Except.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Eight beat an average player.
Everyone else? Nearly four in ten.
Meanwhile, Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh.
Twenty-seven wickets.
Next year, give the analyst the paddle.

items.title: I spent ₹27 crore on one player
items.text:
I spent twenty-seven crore on one cricketer.
My analyst tried to stop me.
I thought he was waving hello.
The room went mad. Then someone checked.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Eight beat an average player.
Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh and took twenty-seven wickets.
Turns out you mostly pay for the hype.
My analyst's got the paddle now.
He's bidding base price.

items.title: The star or the bargain bin?
items.text:
Would you rather have the IPL auction's most expensive player, or three cheap ones?

Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Only eight beat an average player.
Everyone else bought? Nearly four in ten did.
And Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh, then took twenty-seven wickets.
So. The star, or the bargain bin?
Your analyst already knows.
